source: Rules adapted from the Spring Fest 2026 Event Rulebook (IIT Kharagpur) for the fictional CampusFest 2025. Changes from the rulebook are listed under each event.

rules: The judges' decision is final and binding for all events.
If equipment provided by the fest fails, the participant may restart the performance or continue from the point of interruption. Grace time, if needed, is at the judges' discretion.
Penalties are deducted from the team's total judging score.
Going over the time limit can lead to a penalty or disqualification, as the judges decide.
Late submissions may lead to disqualification if the judges so decide.
Script and audio submission deadlines are strict.
CampusFest reserves the right to make final decisions on all matters related to an event, including rules, schedules, changes and disputes, to keep it fair, safe and enjoyable for everyone.
general.championship: College Championship: each scored event carries points. 1st place gets 100% of the event's points, 2nd 60%, 3rd 40%, 4th 20% and 5th 10%. Tied places share the points of the places they occupy equally. The college with the most points after all results wins the Championship trophy.
adapted: The position split is CampusFest's (100/60/40/20/10), not the rulebook's 100/75/50/20.
The rulebook's Hitch Hike rules (direct finale entry for national prelim winners) are dropped: CampusFest has no national prelims.

events.name: Group Dance
events.about: Unite your crew, sync your steps and light up the stage. From Bollywood medleys to thematic acts, show teamwork, precision and flair in a group dance showcase.
rules: Bring the submitted audio on a pen drive or phone as well.
Live music is not allowed.
Stage area is about 20 ft x 25 ft.
If equipment provided fails, the team may repeat from the beginning or from the point of disruption, with the judges' consent.
Accessories, costumes and props are arranged by the team. Submit the list of props with the audio.

submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Group Dance audio: <team name>, <CampusFest ID>".

adapted: Name, dates and submission address changed for CampusFest.
Prelims on 12 Apr and finals on 13 Apr, per the CampusFest program.

events.name: Duet Dance
events.about: Pair up and let your synchronised movement, connection and storytelling take centre stage, in any style.
rules: Bring the submitted audio on a pen drive or phone as well. Live music is not allowed.
Strictly a duet: no extra person on stage at any point.
Any pair is allowed, irrespective of gender. Any dance form is allowed.
Stage area is about 20 ft x 25 ft.
If equipment provided fails, the pair may repeat from the beginning or from the point of disruption, with the judges' consent.
Accessories, costumes and props are arranged by the participants.

submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Duet Dance audio: <participant 1>, <ID 1>, <participant 2>, <ID 2>".

events.name: Shuffle: Group Street Battle
events.about: Breaking, popping, locking, krumping: bring your crew's best moves to a face-off street dance battle.
events.timeLimit: Battles of 5 rounds, 1 minute per crew per round (10 minutes per battle)
rules: Showcase round: crews perform one by one; the judges pick the top crews for the battles.
Battle order is decided by a draw.
Music is provided by the fest at the venue; both crews in a battle dance to the same music.
In each round, up to 4 members of a crew may go, one after another.
A tie may get an extra round.
Accessories, costumes and props are arranged by the crew.

submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Shuffle audio: <college>, <crew name>, <CampusFest ID>".

adapted: Group event only: the rulebook's solo battle is not in the CampusFest program.
Showcase, battles and final happen in one session on 13 Apr, so the rulebook's top-16 bracket is cut to fit.
Not scored for the Championship.

events.name: Stage Play
events.about: Bring your script and your cast to the theatre stage and hold the audience with narrative depth and craft.
events.teamLimit: At least 5, plus at most 1 for music and 3 for lights
events.timeLimit: Prelims 15 minutes, finals 50 minutes (empty stage to empty stage)
rules: Stage area is about 20 ft x 36 ft.
The play can be in English or Hindi.
Mime is allowed. Microphones, backstage mics for narration, lights and a laptop for audio are provided.
Recorded vocals are not allowed; instrumental music only. Bring the music on a pen drive or phone.
If equipment provided fails, the team may repeat from the last scene change or from the point of disruption.
Grace time is at the judges' discretion. Costumes and accessories are arranged by the team.
The organisers are not responsible for items left behind after the performance.
No naked flames or live animals on stage.
Vulgar or disturbing content of any kind stops the performance and disqualifies the team.

submission.what: Script, props list and backing audio
submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Stage Play script: <team name>, <CampusFest ID>".

adapted: Name, dates and submission address changed for CampusFest.
Rulebook 'pre-finals' are CampusFest prelims on 12 Apr; finals on 13 Apr.

events.name: Street Play
events.about: Street plays have long been the voice of the people. Take the pavement stage and make your message land, blending art and activism.
events.timeLimit: Prelims 15 minutes, finals 20 minutes (empty stage to empty stage)
rules: Teams perform at an open-air venue with the audience on all sides.
The play is in Hindi or English.
No fire, water or smoke.
Gulaal or any props used must be cleared by the team within its performance time.
Vulgar or disturbing content of any kind stops the performance and disqualifies the team.
Live music only. Teams bring their own instruments.

submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Street Play script: <team name>, <CampusFest ID>".

events.name: Monologue
events.about: One performer, many characters. Bring a story alive on stage on your own.
events.teamLimit: 1 (solo), plus at most 2 helpers for sound and lights
rules: Two rounds. Present a mono act on any theme.
The act can be in English or Hindi.
You may bring music on a pen drive or phone; recorded vocals are not allowed.
Instrumental music is allowed if you bring your own instruments.
Costumes and accessories are yours to arrange. The organisers provide the venue only and are not responsible for items left in green rooms or on stage.
No naked flames or live animals on stage.
Vulgar or disturbing content of any kind stops the performance and disqualifies the participant.

submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Monologue: <participant name>, <CampusFest ID>".

adapted: Name, dates and submission address changed for CampusFest.

events.name: Western Vocals
events.about: A solo singing stage for voices that can hold a room.
rules: Sing any number of Western (English) songs within the time limit.
You may perform with one instrumental accompanist or a backing track; judging is on the vocals only.
Misconduct, obscenity or foul language leads to disqualification on the spot.

submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Western Vocals: <participant name>, <CampusFest ID>".

adapted: Name, dates and submission address changed for CampusFest.
The rulebook allows Hindi, English or both. CampusFest splits Western and Eastern vocals, so this event is English songs.

events.name: Eastern Vocals
events.noRulesReason: The program borrowed the name Sargam, but the rulebook's Sargam is a fusion band contest, so its rules do not fit a solo vocal event.

events.name: Groups (Bands)
events.about: Rock on. Bring the vocals, riffs and beats, and let the band's chemistry carry the crowd.
events.timeLimit: Prelims 20 minutes, finals 40 minutes (amps on to amps off, sound check included)
rules: Prelims: at least 3 songs of your choice within 20 minutes.
Finals: at least 4 songs within 40 minutes.
Misconduct, obscenity or foul language leads to disqualification on the spot and a ban from future editions of CampusFest.
English and Hindi rock music only.
Provided: one bass amplifier, one lead amplifier, enough microphones and a drum kit (bring your own cymbals and hi-hats if you like).
Bring your own instruments and effects. Programmed music is not allowed.
The fest is not responsible for the failure of any instrument.
adapted: The rulebook's city prelims are dropped; prelims are on campus on 12 Apr and finals on 13 Apr.

events.name: Rapmania
events.about: Verses rule and rhymes reign. A rap battle for lyricists with flow.
rules: Showcase round first; the judges pick the top 8.
Bring a beatboxer, or your beats on a pen drive or phone.
Top 8: a theme is given, with 30 minutes to write before performing on a common beat.
The top 2 meet in a final roast battle; its rules are announced on the spot.
Racist, sexist or offensive slurs lead to immediate disqualification.

submission.what: Lyrics, and a backing track if needed
submission.how: Upload on the CampusFest event page with the subject "Rapmania: <participant name>, <CampusFest ID>".

adapted: All rounds run in one session on 12 Apr.
Hitch Hike winners' entry to the top 8 is dropped.
Not scored for the Championship.

events.name: English Poetry Slam
events.about: Your own words, your own voice. A spoken-word stage in English.
rules: Poems can be on any subject and in any style but must be original, in English.
No props, special costumes, instruments or recorded music.
A poem performed once may not be repeated in later rounds, except in a tie-break. Breaking this disqualifies the poet.
Every poet who performs must be the primary author of the poem.

events.name: Short Film Making
events.about: Tell a story on screen that inspires, provokes or entertains. Entries are made before the fest and screened on 13 Apr.
rules: The film is in Hindi, English or both. No other languages.
Shoot on any device.
A list of situations is released on the CampusFest event page 14 days before the fest. Include at least one.
At least one actor registers at the control tent to confirm the film is the team's own.
The fest is not responsible for playback problems caused by file formats.
No obscenity. Avoid photo animations, slide shows, remixes, spoofs and advertisements.
The judges' and organisers' decision is final and binding.
CampusFest may use entries on social media, with credit to the makers.
Copyrighted content leads to disqualification.

submission.what: The film, as a drive link, in .mpeg or .avi
submission.how: Name the file "Short Film: <team name>, <CampusFest ID>" and submit the link on the CampusFest event page.

events.name: Photostory
events.about: Up to 10 photographs that tell one story. Exhibited and judged on 13 Apr.
rules: An individual event. Any camera, phone included.
Submit at most 10 photographs taken in the stated period, as one PDF with a title and a story of at most 30 words.
The theme is released on the CampusFest event page 20 days before the fest. Photos must be taken after that; EXIF data is checked and plagiarism is dealt with strictly.
Basic editing only: crop, hue and saturation, brightness, contrast. No photo morphing.
The fest is not responsible for technical errors from incompatible files.
